serve.description: `<app>:dev-stack` — the running dev stack (continuous; what `nx serve <app>` runs and an e2e target depends on): a thin wrapper over the stack-free dev engine (`tools/dev/dev serve <app>`): every process the app declares in `.bespunky/dev.json` (the dev-server; the Firebase emulator suite in a Firebase workspace; anything hand-declared) under ONE graceful Ctrl+C, for the current git worktree or any chosen one (--worktree=<branch|slug|path>), on one port offset for every declared port (--port-offset=auto|<n>: the main tree prefers the base ports, each worktree a stable, verified-free block sized from the declaration), reached at `<slug>.localhost` in the shared co-driven browser (--no-shared-browser to serve headless). --skip=<id,…> leaves processes out (--no-emulators is --skip=emulators; the app then opens with ?emulate=none). Options it does not own are forwarded to the app's primary process (buildTarget, host, proxyConfig, ssl, …); --configuration picks the dev-server's build. --dry-run prints the plan.

follow-stack.description: `<app>:serve` — what `nx serve <app>` runs: depends on the continuous `<app>:dev-stack` (flags forwarded) and ends when the stack ends, WITH ITS EXIT STATUS — non-zero, naming the process that died, when the stack failed. Nx reports a continuous task that ends as succeeded when nothing depends on it; this is what depends on it.

serve-preflight.description: Runs before `nx serve <app>` (the `dev-stack` composer depends on it, flags forwarded). When this workspace's Nx already serves the app — where a second `nx serve` would only wait on it and then report a success it never had — it names the running stack, refuses a request for a different stack with the `tools/dev/dev serve` command that starts it beside the running one, or says the run attaches to the running stack (what an e2e target wants).
